# ICML Review

## Summary

The paper studies OJ3, a selective-arbitration policy with D1 fixed as the base and D2/D3 as auxiliary draws. Review occurs only when all three answers are valid and D2 and D3 agree against D1; an anonymous judge then selects one existing candidate, and OJ3 adds a one-versus-two support record relative to GJ3. [ev_p003_b005 · p.3] [ev_p003_b006 · p.3] [ev_p003_b011 · p.3] [ev_p003_b013 · p.3] Evaluation uses two disjoint, category-proportional 1,000-question MMLU-Pro cohorts, with an unchanged replication after the first look, full-denominator scoring, and a conservative one-sided alpha of .025 for the pooled headline test. [ev_p004_b006 · p.4] [ev_p004_b011 · p.4] [ev_p004_b012 · p.4] [ev_p004_b014 · p.4] Pooled OJ3 accuracy was 1,214 of 2,000 versus 1,187 of 2,000 for D1, a gain of 27 correct answers from 33 rescues and six harms; the 1.35-point effect had one-sided p=7.15e-6 and a 95% interval of +0.75 to +1.95 points. [ev_p005_b010 · p.5] [ev_p005_b015 · p.5] [ev_p005_b017 · p.5] [ev_p014_b035 · p.14]

## Strengths

- The paper clearly positions its contribution as an asymmetric preassigned-base routing-and-arbitration policy, with a matched support-hidden judge control rather than a claim that repeated sampling or LLM judging is itself new. [ev_p002_b014 · p.2] [ev_p003_b013 · p.3] [ev_p003_b016 · p.3]
- OJ3 and GJ3 share eligible conflicts, anonymous candidate strings, rotation, model settings, semantic call count, and fallback, with the mechanical support record as the stated treatment difference. [ev_p003_b013 · p.3] [ev_p013_b002 · p.13]
- The confirmatory cohorts are deterministically selected, category-proportional, and disjoint; the replication preserves the policy and analysis choices, while gold labels remain outside solver and judge workspaces. [ev_p004_b006 · p.4] [ev_p004_b011 · p.4] [ev_p011_b022 · p.11]
- The analysis uses full-denominator accuracy, paired exact discordance tests, stratified paired-bootstrap intervals, and a pre-frozen fixed testing sequence with a stopping rule. [ev_p004_b014 · p.4] [ev_p004_b015 · p.4] [ev_p004_b016 · p.4] [ev_p004_b017 · p.4] [ev_p004_b018 · p.4] [ev_p004_b019 · p.4] [ev_p004_b020 · p.4]
- The pooled comparison table places rescues, harms, net correctness, exact-test results, and confidence-interval bounds together, making the main comparisons easy to assess. [ev_p005_b019 · p.5] [ev_p005_b020 · p.5] [ev_p005_b021 · p.5] [ev_p005_b022 · p.5] [ev_p005_b023 · p.5] [ev_p005_b024 · p.5]
- The conflict-set analysis separates routing utility, candidate-set failures, and avoided consensus harms while explicitly declining to attribute the OJ3-versus-GJ3 increment causally to support counts. [ev_p006_b004 · p.6] [ev_p006_b005 · p.6] [ev_p006_b013 · p.6]

## Weaknesses

- OJ3 did not establish superiority over SC3 or GJ3: its five-answer advantage over SC3 was not rejected, the GJ3 comparison was not formally reached, and the observed three-answer GJ3 difference was nonsignificant. [ev_p005_b018 · p.5] [ev_p014_b036 · p.14] [ev_p014_b037 · p.14] [ev_p008_b004 · p.8]
- Because GJ3 and OJ3 each used one separate complete-file judge session, their realized contrast cannot distinguish the support-record treatment from judge-session or within-session context variation. [ev_p003_b016 · p.3] [ev_p004_b008 · p.4] [ev_p004_b009 · p.4] [ev_p006_b006 · p.6]
- The practical gain is modest relative to compute: the 1.35-point improvement over D1 required 3.53 times its tokens, while token matching does not establish exact monetary cost or wall-time latency. [ev_p006_b015 · p.6] [ev_p007_b013 · p.7] [ev_p008_b005 · p.8]
- The proposed operating boundary remains qualitative, and the negative legal comparison cannot provide a predictive explanation because domain, task, prompt, and label structure all changed together. [ev_p007_b002 · p.7] [ev_p007_b008 · p.7] [ev_p007_b009 · p.7] [ev_p008_b006 · p.8]

## Questions for Authors

1. Can the authors repeat the complete pipeline on the same MMLU-Pro items and report between-session variation in D1 accuracy, trigger rate, OJ3-versus-D1 effects, and OJ3-versus-GJ3 effects? [ev_p004_b009 · p.4] [ev_p005_b007 · p.5] [ev_p008_b002 · p.8]
   Assessment change: Stable effects and conflict rates across identical-item repetitions would raise the soundness score and overall acceptance assessment by addressing unestimated pipeline repeatability; substantial sensitivity to session realization would lower both.
2. Can GJ3 and OJ3 be evaluated over multiple paired or counterbalanced judge sessions on the same frozen conflicts, with the support record as the only treatment difference? [ev_p003_b016 · p.3] [ev_p004_b008 · p.4] [ev_p004_b009 · p.4] [ev_p006_b006 · p.6] [ev_p008_b004 · p.8]
   Assessment change: A reproducible positive OJ3-versus-GJ3 effect under repeated paired or counterbalanced judge sessions would raise the soundness, originality, and significance scores and strengthen acceptance by supporting an incremental support-annotation effect; a null or session-sensitive result would not support that mechanism.
3. Can the authors report cached and uncached monetary costs and deployment-relevant latency for the 1.35-percentage-point gain, rather than token totals alone? [ev_p006_b015 · p.6] [ev_p007_b013 · p.7] [ev_p008_b005 · p.8]
   Assessment change: Deployment-level evidence showing a favorable accuracy–cost trade-off would raise the significance score and overall acceptance assessment; evidence that monetary cost or latency dominates the 1.35-point gain would lower them.
4. Can the authors test answer determinacy while holding domain, task, prompt, and label structure fixed to isolate the proposed explanation for the negative legal result? [ev_p007_b002 · p.7] [ev_p007_b009 · p.7] [ev_p008_b006 · p.8]
   Assessment change: A matched experiment identifying an effect of answer determinacy would raise the originality and significance scores and strengthen acceptance by providing a predictive boundary for the method; failure to isolate such an effect would leave the generalization assessment limited.
5. Can the authors establish a reuse basis for the five legacy records or exclude them, and specify the governance criteria and re-identification review required before any item-level release? [ev_p008_b006 · p.8] [ev_p008_b009 · p.8] [ev_p011_b024 · p.11] [ev_p011_b025 · p.11]
   Assessment change: Documenting a valid reuse basis or removing the affected records, together with specified governance and re-identification safeguards, could improve the ethical acceptability and overall acceptance assessment; unresolved reuse status and residual risk would sustain the concern and could lower acceptance.

## Limitations

Confirmation covers one model, one runtime, and one primary multiple-choice benchmark; the benchmark may have appeared in model training, and “fresh” does not mean post-training or contamination-free. [ev_p007_b015 · p.7] The pipeline was not rerun on identical items, so the paired inference conditions on the realized whole-file sessions and does not estimate between-session repeatability; the large D2 discrepancy across cohorts raises a repeatability concern without establishing its cause. [ev_p004_b009 · p.4] [ev_p005_b007 · p.5] [ev_p008_b002 · p.8] All candidate and judge sessions use the same model family, so separate sessions do not remove correlated model-level errors; both available candidates were wrong on 20 of 68 conflicts. [ev_p008_b003 · p.8] Only 68 of 2,000 questions triggered arbitration, limiting precision for the OJ3-versus-GJ3 comparison and leaving the incremental support-annotation effect unresolved. [ev_p008_b004 · p.8] The legal reserve changes domain, task, prompt, and label structure simultaneously, so it cannot identify why transfer failed or support conclusions about legal question answering with complete statutes and facts. [ev_p008_b006 · p.8]

## Overall Recommendation

3/6

## Confidence

4/5

## Ethical Concerns

Verified ethical concerns: Five selected legacy lawlaw records lack recoverable reuse metadata, and the transformations do not comprehensively de-identify narrative facts, leaving residual re-identification risk; item-level materials are withheld pending governance review.
